record.one_liner: Atlassian's issue and project tracking product for software and business teams, with a cloud REST API for issues, projects, workflows, users and more.
record.auth_notes: Basic auth with Atlassian account email + API token (Authorization: Basic base64(email:token)); passwords deprecated. OAuth 2.0 (3LO) is documented for third-party apps (scopes, offline_access refresh tokens rotating, 90-day inactivity expiry). Forge apps use OAuth 2.0 and Connect apps use JWT. Per the docs, apps that collect customers' API tokens or have customers create individual 3LO apps violate Atlassian's security requirements; use a single distributable 3LO app. Not fetched: Jira Data Center PATs and scoped API tokens, so those are unconfirmed.
record.access_notes: An Atlassian account can generate an API token, and a developer can create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the developer console, both self-serve. The API runs against a Jira Cloud site; I did not verify the free-plan details on a fetched page, but the rate-limit page lists a Free edition. Distributing a 3LO app to other users works without Marketplace listing, but users see an 'unreviewed integration' warning until Atlassian approves it.
record.blocker: Points-based hourly quota (65,000 points/hour shared global pool for most apps) plus per-second and per-issue write limits; HTTP 429 on exceed. Distributable OAuth apps show an unreviewed warning until Atlassian approves. Customer-supplied API tokens in a multi-tenant app are against Atlassian's requirements, so use one 3LO app. 3LO refresh tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity.

evidence.auth: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/basic-auth-for-rest-apis/ (email + API token basic auth; Forge OAuth2, Connect JWT); https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/oauth-2-3lo-apps/ (3LO flow, scopes, refresh tokens, review warning)
evidence.access: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/oauth-2-3lo-apps/ (create app in developer console, share via Distribution; unreviewed warning)
evidence.api: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rate-limiting/ (REST limits, GraphQL mentioned as later enforcement). The REST v3 intro and GraphQL pages failed to fetch, so breadth and GraphQL are inferred from other pages and my background knowledge.
